chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not sit (in a specific manner) between the two prostrations."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِقْعَاءً: Sitting on the heels with knees upright (a specific posture)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting between the two prostrations in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* via the chain of Samaanah and Abu Basir, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific etiquette of the inter-prostration sitting. It distinguishes the recommended *tawarruk* posture from *iq'a* (sitting upright on heels), a detail that became central to Shia fiqh in distinguishing their prayer style from other schools, emphasizing humility and stability during the brief pause in prayer.
